The Difference Between White Label and Grey Label Forex
To understand the difference between white label and grey label forex setups properly, it helps to look at a few specific areas.
Control Over Trading Conditions

On a white label, many of your settings sit under the main server’s oversight. You may be able to set some spreads and commissions, but leverage limits, symbol settings and group structures are often restricted.
On a grey label, those decisions are largely yours. You can build your own groups, set your own spreads and markups, adjust leverage and decide which instruments each client type can trade.
Manager and Admin Access
White label brokers usually get a limited back office view. Enough to see clients and accounts, but not much more.
Grey label brokers get proper manager terminal access. Your dealing team can monitor exposure, adjust positions, manage groups and react to market conditions without waiting on anyone else.
Risk Management
This is one of the biggest practical differences. With a white label, risk is often handled at the main server level, which limits how you can run your book.

With a grey label, you have far more flexibility. You can decide how much flow to route to liquidity providers, how much to keep internally and how to treat different client groups. For brokers who want to grow revenue seriously, that matters a lot.
Branding
Both models let you put your name on the platform, the client portal and your website. Traders won’t see the provider behind you in either case. Branding isn’t really where they differ.
Cost

A white label is the cheaper option, both in setup fee and monthly fee. A grey label costs more because you’re getting more control and more server resources. Even so, both sit well below the cost of a full licence and your own infrastructure.
Speed to Launch
Both can go live quickly once your paperwork is ready. A white label is sometimes a little faster simply because there’s less to configure.

Can I switch from an MT5 white label to a grey label?
Yes. Since both run on our infrastructure, we can move your groups and client accounts across with minimal disruption. Many brokers make this step once their volumes grow.
Grey Label Forex Price Guide: What You’ll Pay and Why

A grey label is a bigger step than a white label, so it makes sense that brokers want to understand the numbers properly before committing. The trouble is, most providers keep pricing vague until you’re deep into a sales call.

This page does the opposite. It explains what goes into a grey label forex price, how setup and monthly fees work, where the costs can rise and how to keep them under control. By the end, you should have a realistic sense of your budget before speaking to anyone.
Why a Grey Label Costs More Than a White Label
It’s a fair question. Both run on existing MetaTrader infrastructure, so why the price gap?

The answer is control. With a grey label, you get your own manager and admin access, independent groups, custom trading conditions and much more say over risk. That means more server resources, more configuration work and more hands-on support from our side. You’re paying for independence, and for most growing brokers, it pays for itself fairly quickly.
Still Far Below a Full Licence

To keep things in perspective, a grey label remains a fraction of what a full MetaTrader server licence costs once you add hosting, integrations and an in-house technical team. You get much of the freedom without that weight.
How Grey Label Pricing Is Structured

The Setup Fee

A one-time payment that covers getting you live. Server configuration, manager and admin access, branding, groups and symbols, liquidity bridge connection, CRM and payment integrations if included, and full testing with your team.
The Grey Label Monthly Fee

The grey label monthly fee covers keeping everything running. Server access and hosting, platform updates, routine configuration changes, monitoring and support from people who know MetaTrader properly. It’s fixed and agreed before you sign.
Optional Add-Ons
Extra tools you can add when you’re ready. Copy trading, PAMM and MAM, additional payment gateways, advanced risk plugins or a second platform. None of these are required at launch.

MT4 Grey Label Pricing Compared With MT5

What moves the price more is everything around the platform. The number of symbols, how many groups you need, which integrations you add and whether you want both platforms running together.
When MT4 Is the Better Value
If your traders are mainly forex focused and rely on MT4 indicators and EAs, an MT4 grey label keeps them happy and keeps your setup simple.
When MT5 Is Worth It
If you plan to offer indices, commodities, stocks or crypto CFDs, MT5 handles everything in one place. Paying for MT5 now usually works out cheaper than migrating later.
Is There Such a Thing as a Cheap Forex Grey Label?

Yes and no. You’ll find providers advertising a cheap forex grey label at prices that look almost too good. Sometimes they’re genuine. More often, the low headline figure is followed by extra charges for reports, plugins, configuration changes or support hours.
What to Check Before You Sign

Ask exactly what the monthly fee covers. Ask whether routine changes cost extra. Ask what support looks like at 2am during a market spike. And ask for every fee in writing. A cheap offer that can’t answer these clearly usually ends up costing more.
How We Keep Costs Low Without Cutting Corners

We price our packages so new grey label brokers can afford them, and we only include what you’ll actually use. Start lean, then add tools as your volumes grow. Your costs scale with your revenue rather than running ahead of it.
Costs Outside Your Grey Label

blocks.text: Upgrade Grey Label to Admin License and Take Full Ownership of Your Brokerage

A grey label is a great place to grow. You’ve got your brand, your own groups and real control over trading conditions. But at some point, many brokers start to feel the ceiling. Volumes are up, the team is bigger, and the idea of running your own server, under your own licence, starts to sound less like a dream and more like the obvious next step.

If that’s where you are, this page explains what it means to upgrade grey label to admin level, what changes, what it costs in effort and money, and how we help you make the move without disrupting your clients.
What an Admin License Actually Means

On a grey label, you work inside a server that’s licensed and controlled by your provider. You have manager access, but the deepest settings, server configuration and licence ownership stay with them.

With an admin licence, the server is yours. You hold the licence, you get full administrator access and you decide how every part of the environment is configured. Plugins, server settings, data feeds, gateways, backups, all of it.
The Practical Difference

On a grey label, you run your business on someone else’s platform. With an admin licence, the platform itself belongs to you. That brings more freedom, more responsibility and a stronger position when talking to banks, regulators and investors.
Signs You’re Ready to Upgrade
Not every broker should make this move, and certainly not too early. Here are the signals that usually mean the timing is right.
Your Volumes Justify the Cost
When your monthly grey label fees, plus the revenue you’re leaving on the table, start to approach what owning your own server would cost, the maths begins to favour an upgrade.
You Need Deeper Customisation
Maybe you want plugins your provider can’t run, custom server-side logic, or integrations with tools that need administrator access. Those are hard to achieve on a grey label.
Regulators or Partners Expect It
Some licensing authorities, banking partners and institutional clients prefer, or require, that a broker owns its trading infrastructure. An admin licence can make those conversations much easier.
You Have the Team to Support It
Running your own server means taking on more technical responsibility. If you’ve got, or can hire, people who understand MetaTrader administration, you’re in a much better position to upgrade.
MT4 Admin License Upgrade: How It Works
An MT4 admin license upgrade sounds complicated, and done badly, it can be. Done properly, your traders barely notice anything happened.
Planning
We start by mapping your current setup. Groups, symbols, trading conditions, plugins, CRM connections, payment flows and liquidity routes. Nothing gets moved until we know exactly what’s there.
Licensing and Server Setup
We guide you through acquiring your own licence and set up your new server environment, configured to match what you already run, plus any improvements you’ve been wanting.
Migration
Client accounts, history, balances and open positions are moved across, usually over a weekend when markets are closed. We test everything thoroughly before reopening.
Go Live and Handover
Your team gets full administrator access and training on what’s new. Our support continues afterwards, so you’re never left managing a new server alone.
Grow From Grey Label to White Label: Clearing Up the Terms
You may see the phrase grow from grey label to white label and wonder if it’s backwards. It depends on who’s talking.
In everyday broker conversations, a white label usually means the lightest entry option, a branded platform on someone else’s server with limited control. That’s how we use it elsewhere on this site.

But MetaQuotes, the company behind MetaTrader, uses “White Label” to describe its full branded server licence. In that sense, growing from a grey label to a white label means moving to your own licensed server, which is exactly what this page is about.
Why the Confusion Matters

If a provider offers you a “white label upgrade,” ask exactly what you’ll own. Is it a full licence in your company’s name with administrator access? Or a branded platform on their server with less control than you have now? The answer changes everything.
What You Gain After Upgrading

Full control over server configuration and plugins. Ownership of your licence and trading infrastructure. Freedom to choose your own hosting, data centres and technology partners. A stronger profile with regulators, banks and investors. And no ceiling on how far you can customise your brokerage.
What You Take On

More responsibility for uptime, security and maintenance. Higher upfront licence costs. A need for in-house or outsourced technical expertise. We’ll be honest about all of this, because an upgrade only makes sense if you’re ready for both sides of it.
How We Support Your Upgrade

Because we already know your grey label setup inside out, we’re well placed to handle the move. We plan the migration, set up and configure your new server, transfer your clients and data, and stay on as your technical partner afterwards if you’d like us to.
Some clients keep us on for full server management. Others take most of it in-house and use us for specialist support. Either works.
Ready to Own Your Infrastructure?
If your brokerage has outgrown shared infrastructure, it may be time to upgrade grey label to admin and take full ownership of your platform.

Whether you’re planning an MT4 admin license upgrade or exploring what it means to grow from grey label to white label under MetaQuotes’ licensing, we’ll walk you through the costs, the timeline and the risks honestly. Tell us where your brokerage is today, and we’ll help you plan the next step. Get in touch.
Frequently Asked Questions
How long does an upgrade to an admin licence take?

It depends on the licensing process and the size of your setup. The migration itself is usually done over a weekend, but planning and licence approval can take several weeks. We’ll give you a realistic timeline at the start.
Will my clients notice the change?
If it’s planned well, very little. Accounts, balances and history move across, and clients log in to a new server address. We help you communicate the change clearly so nobody is caught off guard.
Can I upgrade from MT5 as well as MT4?
Yes. While this page focuses on the MT4 admin licence upgrade, we support the same move for MT5 brokers, or for brokers running both platforms.
Do I need my own technical team after upgrading?
You’ll need someone responsible for server administration. That can be an in-house team, us, or a mix of both. We’ll help you decide what makes sense for your size.
MT4 and MT5 Admin License: Own Your MetaTrader Server Outright

Every broker starts somewhere. Some begin on a white label, others on a grey label, and a few go straight for the real thing. Whichever route you take, there’s a point where owning your trading infrastructure becomes the logical choice.

An admin licence means the MetaTrader server is yours. Your company holds the licence, your team has full administrator access and every decision about how the platform runs sits with you. This page explains what that involves, who it suits and how we help you set it up properly.
What Is an MT4 or MT5 Admin License?
It’s a full server licence for MetaTrader, issued in your company’s name. Unlike white or grey label arrangements, you aren’t working inside someone else’s environment. You own it.

With an MT4 admin license or MT5 admin license, you get administrator access to the server itself. That covers server settings, plugins, data feeds, gateways, backups, security and every group and symbol on the platform. Nothing needs approval from a provider above you.
Admin Access vs Manager Access

On a grey label, you work with manager access. That’s enough to run groups, trading conditions and client accounts. Admin access goes deeper. You control the server configuration, install plugins, connect any gateway you choose and decide how the infrastructure is hosted and maintained.
Why Brokers Choose Their Own MetaTrader License
Holding your own MetaTrader license isn’t right for everyone. But for brokers at the right stage, it changes a lot.
Complete Independence
No provider limits on plugins, integrations or server settings. If you want to run custom risk tools, connect a specific liquidity bridge or build server-side logic, you can.
Stronger Credibility
Banks, payment providers, regulators and institutional clients often take a broker more seriously when it owns its infrastructure. It signals commitment and long-term stability.
Better Long-Term Economics
The upfront cost is higher, but there are no ongoing grey label fees tied to a provider’s server. For brokers with solid volumes, owning the licence often works out cheaper over a few years.
Full Control Over Your Data
Client data, trading history and server logs sit on infrastructure you control. That matters for compliance, audits and peace of mind.
MT4 Admin License or MT5 Admin License?
Both give you full ownership. The right one depends on your traders and your product plans.
MT4 Admin License

Best for brokers with a forex-focused audience that relies on MT4 indicators and expert advisors. It’s familiar, stable and still widely used. One thing to note: new MT4 licences have become harder to obtain as MetaQuotes focuses on MT5, so availability is worth checking early.
MT5 Admin License

The natural choice for most new licence holders. MT5 handles forex, metals, indices, stocks, futures and crypto CFDs in one platform, supports both hedging and netting, and is where new features and integrations arrive first.
Running Both
Some brokers hold both licences so they can serve every type of trader. It adds cost and admin work, but it removes any platform barrier for new clients.
What Comes With a MetaTrader License for Brokers
A MetaTrader license for brokers gives you the core server and platform. To turn it into a working brokerage, you’ll typically need several more pieces around it.
Core Components
The trading server, administrator and manager terminals, client terminals for desktop, web and mobile, and the data and history servers your platform runs on.
What You’ll Need Alongside It

Hosting in a reliable data centre, a liquidity bridge, a forex CRM and client portal, payment gateway integrations, risk management tools, backup and disaster recovery, and people who know how to keep it all running. We can help with every one of these.
How We Help You Set Up Your Admin License
Owning a server is one thing. Getting it configured, connected and stable is where most brokers need support.
Licensing Guidance
We walk you through the licensing process, the documents you’ll need and what to expect, so there are no surprises along the way.
Server Setup and Hosting
We set up your server environment, configure it for performance and security, and help you choose hosting that suits your markets and latency needs.
Integrations
Liquidity bridge, CRM, client portal, payment gateways and plugins, all configured and tested together before you go live.
Ongoing Server Management
After launch, we can manage the server for you completely, support your in-house team, or step in only when you need specialist help. You choose the level.
Is an Admin License Right for You Yet?

We’ll be straight with you. An admin licence is a big commitment. It suits brokers with steady volumes, a clear growth plan, and either an in-house technical team or a trusted partner to manage the server.

If you’re just starting out or still testing a market, a white label or grey label is usually the smarter first move. Many of our clients start there and move to their own licence once the numbers justify it. We’ll help you work out which stage you’re at.
Take Full Ownership of Your Trading Platform
An MT4 admin license or MT5 admin license puts your brokerage on infrastructure that truly belongs to you. More control, more credibility and more room to build exactly the business you want.
Frequently Asked Questions
How much does an MT4 or MT5 admin licence cost?

It depends on the licence type, your hosting choices, integrations and support level. Licence fees are set by MetaQuotes, and setup and management costs vary by provider. Share your plans with us and we’ll give you a clear, itemised estimate.
How long does it take to get my own MetaTrader licence?
The licensing process can take several weeks, depending on your documents and MetaQuotes’ review. Server setup and integrations usually run in parallel, so you can launch soon after approval.
Can I move my existing grey label clients to my own licence?
Yes. We can migrate client accounts, balances and trading history from a grey label to your new server, usually over a weekend, with minimal disruption to your traders.
Do I need a regulatory licence before applying?

Requirements vary. MetaQuotes may ask for company and regulatory documents during the process, and your target markets will have their own rules. Your legal advisor should confirm what applies to you.
MT4 Admin License for Brokers Who Want Full Control of Their Platform

MT4 is still the platform a huge number of forex traders reach for first. It’s familiar, dependable and backed by years of custom indicators and expert advisors. For a broker whose clients live on MT4, owning the server behind it can be a serious advantage.

An MT4 admin license puts that server in your hands. Your company holds the licence, your team has administrator access and every decision about how the platform runs is yours. This page covers what that involves, what it costs, how setup works and what you should know before you commit.
What an MT4 Admin License Gives You
With your own licence, you’re no longer operating inside someone else’s environment. The MT4 server, its configuration and everything running on it belong to your brokerage.
Administrator-Level Access
You control server settings, plugins, gateways, data feeds, backups and security. Your team can make changes whenever needed without asking a provider for permission.
Full Control Over Trading Operations
Groups, symbols, spreads, swaps, leverage, trading sessions and execution settings are all set by you. You can build your offer exactly the way your clients need it.
Ownership of Client Data
Trading history, client records and server logs sit on infrastructure your company controls. That makes compliance reviews and audits far more straightforward.
An Important Note on MT4 Server License Availability
Before you plan around an MT4 server license, there’s something you should know. MetaQuotes has focused heavily on MT5 for several years and has largely stopped issuing brand new MT4 server licences.

That doesn’t always rule MT4 out. Some brokers already hold MT4 licences, and in certain cases there may be other routes worth exploring. But it does mean availability needs checking early, before you build your plans around it.
Why We Mention This Upfront
Some providers skip over this until well into the process. We’d rather you know at the start, so you can weigh MT4 against MT5 properly and avoid wasting time or money.
The MT5 Alternative

If a new MT4 licence isn’t available for your situation, an MT5 admin licence is usually the natural option. MT5 supports forex alongside metals, indices, stocks and futures, and most MT4 traders adapt to it within a few days.
Understanding MT4 Admin Cost
The MT4 admin cost is made up of several pieces, and it’s worth looking at each one rather than a single headline figure.
Licence Fees
Where an MT4 licence is available, the licence fee itself is set by MetaQuotes or determined by the specific arrangement. This is usually the largest upfront cost.
Hosting and Infrastructure
Your server needs to run in a reliable data centre, ideally close to your liquidity providers for low latency. Hosting costs depend on location, performance requirements and backup needs.
Integrations
Liquidity bridge, forex CRM, client portal, payment gateways and risk management plugins all add to the total. Some brokers already have several of these in place.
Ongoing Management
Someone has to keep the server healthy. That could be your own team, a managed service from us, or a combination. Monthly costs depend on how much support you need.
Getting an Accurate Figure
Because so much depends on your setup, the most reliable way to get a real number is to share your plans with us. We’ll send back an itemised estimate showing exactly where the money goes.
MT4 Admin Setup: How the Process Works
A good MT4 admin setup is mostly about careful planning. Rushing it is how brokers end up with downtime and unhappy clients.
Step One: Assessment
We look at your current position. Do you already hold a licence? Are you moving from a grey label? Which markets are you serving? That shapes the whole plan.
Step Two: Infrastructure
We help you choose hosting, set up the server environment and configure it for performance, stability and security.
Step Three: Configuration
Groups, symbols, trading conditions, plugins and gateways are set up to match your business model. If you’re moving from a grey label, we replicate your existing setup and improve on it where needed.
Step Four: Integrations and Testing
Your CRM, client portal, payments and liquidity bridge are connected and tested together. Your team runs through real scenarios before anything goes live.
Step Five: Launch and Support
You go live with full administrator access. We stay involved for as long as you want, from full server management to occasional specialist help.
Who an MT4 Admin License Suits

Owning an MT4 server makes most sense for established brokers with strong MT4 audiences, firms already holding an MT4 licence who need better setup and management, and grey label brokers whose volumes now justify their own infrastructure. You’ll also want either a technical team or a reliable partner to manage the server day to day.
If you’re new to the industry, a grey label is often the better starting point. We’ll tell you honestly which fits.
Take Full Control of Your MT4 Brokerage
An MT4 admin license gives you ownership, control and credibility that shared infrastructure can’t match. But it’s a big step, and it deserves honest advice and careful planning.

Can I still get a new MT4 admin licence?

New MT4 server licences are very limited, as MetaQuotes now focuses on MT5. Availability depends on your situation, so it’s best to check early. If MT4 isn’t possible, we’ll walk you through MT5 as an alternative.
I already have an MT4 licence. Can you manage it for me?
Yes. We can take over setup, hosting, configuration and ongoing management of an existing MT4 server, or support your in-house team where they need help.
Can I run MT5 alongside my MT4 server?
Yes. Many brokers keep MT4 for existing clients and add MT5 for new instruments and newer traders. We can set up and manage both.
How long does MT4 admin setup take?
If you already hold a licence, server setup and integrations can often be completed within a few weeks. Migrations from a grey label are usually done over a weekend to avoid disrupting traders.
MT5 Admin License for Brokers Ready to Own Their Trading Infrastructure

MT5 has become the platform most new brokerages build on. It handles forex, metals, indices, stocks, futures and crypto CFDs in one place, and it’s where MetaQuotes now puts almost all of its development effort. For brokers planning to grow, owning that platform outright is a serious step forward.

What an MT5 Admin License Gives You
With your own licence, the server and everything running on it belong to your brokerage. You make the decisions, your team holds the keys.
Full Administrator Access

Server settings, plugins, gateways, data feeds, backups and security are all under your control. Your team can act immediately when something needs changing, rather than raising a request and waiting.
Freedom to Build Your Product

Choose which asset classes to offer, how each symbol is configured and how trading sessions run. Set spreads, commissions, swaps and leverage by group, by region or by instrument. Your offer can be as simple or as detailed as your business needs.
Ownership of Your Data
Client records, trading history and server logs sit on infrastructure your company controls. That makes regulatory reporting, audits and data protection much easier to manage.
Why MT5 Is the Licence Most Brokers Choose Today
Unlike MT4, an MT5 server license is still actively issued and supported by MetaQuotes, which makes it the practical choice for most brokers moving to their own infrastructure.
True Multi-Asset Trading
One server can carry forex, metals, energies, indices, stocks, futures and crypto CFDs. As your clients ask for new markets, you add symbols rather than new platforms.
Hedging and Netting Support
MT5 lets you run both hedging and netting account types. That means you can serve traditional forex traders and those used to exchange-style position handling from the same server.
Better Performance and Tools
The multi-threaded strategy tester, more timeframes, more order types, market depth and a built-in economic calendar all make MT5 attractive to active and algorithmic traders.
A Platform That Keeps Improving
New features, gateways and integrations land on MT5 first. Owning an MT5 server means your brokerage stays current without a painful migration down the line.
Understanding MT5 Admin Cost

Integrations

Server Management

Getting a Real Number

MT5 Admin Setup: Our Step-by-Step Process

Step Six: Go Live and Ongoing Support
You launch with full administrator access. Afterwards, we can manage the server completely, support your team, or step in only when needed.
Who Should Get an MT5 Admin License?

It’s a strong fit for grey label brokers whose volumes now justify their own server, multi-asset brokers who need deep control over symbols and sessions, firms entering regulated markets where owning infrastructure matters, and MT4 brokers ready to move to a modern platform.
If you’re still testing a market or building your first client base, a white label or grey label is often the smarter first step. We’ll give you an honest view of which suits you.
Own the Platform Your Brokerage Runs On
An MT5 admin license gives you the control, credibility and flexibility that shared setups can’t offer. It’s a big step, and it deserves careful planning and honest advice.

Yes. We migrate accounts, balances and trading history, usually over a weekend when markets are closed, so your traders face minimal disruption.

A Book vs B Book vs Hybrid: Choosing the Right Execution Model for Your Brokerage

Ask any new broker what keeps them up at night and execution often comes up. Not because it’s complicated to set up, but because the choice you make shapes your revenue, your risk and how your clients experience every trade.

What Is A Book Execution?

With a book execution, client orders are passed straight through to your liquidity providers. When a client buys EUR/USD, your broker places a matching trade with the market. You’re the middle person, not the counterparty.
How A Book Brokers Make Money
Revenue comes from spread markups and commissions on each trade. Whether the client wins or loses, you earn from their trading activity.
The Advantages

There’s no direct conflict of interest, since you don’t profit when clients lose. Your market risk stays low because positions are offset with providers. And some professional traders and institutional clients specifically look for brokers running this model.
The Downsides

Margins per trade are thinner. You need decent volumes to build meaningful revenue. Your costs depend on what your liquidity providers charge, and some flow, like aggressive scalping, can be expensive to pass on.
What Is a B Book Forex Broker?
A b book forex broker keeps client trades in-house rather than sending them to the market. The broker becomes the counterparty. If a client buys, the broker effectively takes the opposite side.
How B Book Brokers Make Money
Revenue comes from spreads and commissions, plus net client losses. Statistically, a large share of retail traders lose over time, which is why this model can be profitable.
The Advantages
Higher potential revenue per client. No liquidity costs on internalised trades. Faster execution, since orders don’t leave your server.
The Downsides

There’s a built-in conflict of interest, because you benefit when clients lose. Profitable traders become a real cost and risk. A run of winning clients, or a sharp market move, can hurt your balance sheet. And regulators in many jurisdictions watch B book practices closely, so transparency and fair treatment are essential.
Doing It Responsibly

Running a B book doesn’t have to mean treating clients unfairly. Responsible brokers execute honestly, never manipulate prices, disclose their execution model and keep enough capital to cover exposure. Reputation in this industry travels fast.
How the Forex Hybrid Model Works
The forex hybrid model combines both approaches. Some client flow goes to liquidity providers. Some stays in-house. The split is decided by rules your dealing team sets.
Typical Ways to Split Flow

By client type, so consistently profitable traders are routed out and smaller retail accounts stay internal. By trade size, so large orders go to the market to limit exposure. By instrument, so certain volatile symbols are always hedged. Or by overall exposure, so once internal risk reaches a set level, new trades are passed through.
Why Many Brokers Choose Hybrid

It balances revenue with risk. You keep the income potential of internalising some flow, while protecting yourself from the clients and positions that could cause real damage. It’s flexible too, so you can adjust as your client base changes.
What It Requires
A hybrid model only works with good data and the right tools. Your dealing team needs to see client behaviour, exposure and profitability clearly, and adjust routing rules confidently.

doc-36.title: MetaTrader Grey Label vs White Label: Which Is Best for Your Forex Brokerage?

blocks.text: MetaTrader Grey Label vs White Label: Which Is Best for Your Forex Brokerage?

Most brokers don’t start out asking about server architecture. They start with a budget, a launch date, and a rough sense that they need MetaTrader because that’s what their traders already use. Then someone mentions grey label, someone else says white label, and the conversation gets murky fast.

So let’s untangle it. The MetaTrader grey label vs white label question isn’t really about which one is better. It comes down to how much of your brokerage you want to own on day one, and how much you’re happy to rent.
A Quick Bit of Background First

MetaQuotes, the company behind MT4 and MT5, sells full server licenses directly. They’re expensive and come with strict requirements, and new MT4 licenses are no longer issued at all. That gap is why white label and grey label models exist. Providers who already hold full licenses carve out access and offer it to newer brokers at a much lower entry cost.
Both routes put your brand on the terminal your clients log into. The difference is in what’s happening behind that login screen.
What a White Label Actually Gives You

With a white label, you’re basically a tenant. The provider runs the server, and your brokerage sits on it as a branded segment alongside other brokers. Your clients see your name and logo. You get a manager terminal, reporting tools, and the ability to open accounts and set up some trading groups.
Where White Label Works Well

Speed is the big one. A white label can often go live in a couple of weeks because there’s nothing to build. It’s cheaper too, both upfront and month to month, which matters a lot when you’re still finding out whether your marketing can bring in funded clients.
It also suits brokers who’d rather not think about infrastructure at all. The provider handles uptime, backups, security patches and plugin updates.
Where It Starts to Pinch

The trade-off is control. You’re working inside someone else’s setup. Want a bridge to a liquidity provider they don’t support? You might wait, or you might go without. Need a custom plugin, or a different approach to execution and risk? That’s usually something you have to request, not something you decide.

Then there’s the shared server. If the host has an outage, every broker on it has one too. And your client data sits on infrastructure you don’t control, which can make some regulators and institutional partners uneasy.
What Changes With a Grey Label

A grey label sits in the middle ground between a white label and a full license. You get your own dedicated MetaTrader server instance, usually MT5 these days. It runs under the provider’s master license but is kept separate from other brokers.

In practice, that means admin access, not just manager access. You configure symbols, groups, swaps, margin rules and execution settings yourself. You pick your liquidity providers and bridges, and you can install plugins that fit how you want to run your book. Your client data stays on your own server.
Who Grey Label Suits

Brokers who already have some traction usually get the most out of it. If you have a client base, a clear plan for A-book, B-book or hybrid execution, and a team that knows its way around a MetaTrader admin panel, a grey label lets you run things your way.
It’s also a sensible next step if you’ve outgrown a white label but aren’t ready for a full license, or can’t get one.
The Extra Cost and Work

More control means more work. Setup and monthly fees are higher than for a white label. You’ll need people, in-house or outsourced, who can manage the server, watch risk and keep the configuration clean. Launch also takes longer because there’s real setup involved.
The Part That Hits Your Margins
This is where the difference grey vs white label setups make really shows: how much room you have to shape your revenue.

On a white label, spreads, markups, commission structures and hedging all sit within limits the host sets. On a grey label, you set those limits yourself. That doesn’t make it automatically more profitable. A badly configured grey label can lose money faster than a well-run white label ever would. But the ceiling is higher, and the decisions are yours.
A quick side-by-side:
Control: white label gives you manager access, grey label gives you admin access to your own server
Liquidity: white label ties you to the host’s options, grey label lets you choose
Launch time: white label is usually quicker
Cost: white label is cheaper to start and to run
Data: on a white label it sits on a shared server, on a grey label it sits on yours
So Which One Should You Pick?
Honestly, it depends on where your brokerage is today, not where you hope it’ll be in three years.

If you’re new, testing a market or working with a tight budget, a white label is usually the smarter place to start. You get to market quickly, see what your clients actually trade, and keep costs under control. Plenty of successful brokers started this way and moved on later.

If you already have clients, a defined execution model and some technical depth in-house, a grey label starts to make more sense. The extra cost earns its keep once the host’s restrictions are costing you money or clients.
Before you decide, it’s worth asking yourself a few things:
How many funded clients do you realistically expect in the first year?
Do you have someone who can manage a MetaTrader server, or will you need to hire?
Are you tied to particular liquidity providers?
What does your regulator expect around data storage and server control?

If most of your answers are “not yet” or “not sure,” start with a white label. If they’re “yes, and it’s already a problem,” look seriously at a grey label. In the end, the difference grey vs white label models come down to is simple: who holds the keys.
Conclusion

The MetaTrader grey label vs white label decision isn’t permanent. Lots of brokers launch on a white label, build volume, then move to a grey label once they need more control. That path is perfectly reasonable, and often cheaper than jumping straight into infrastructure you’re not ready to run.
If you’re thinking about the move, the team at MetaGreyLabel can show you what a grey label setup would look like for your brokerage, and whether now is the right time to make it.

blocks.text: Step-by-Step Guide to Setting Up a MetaTrader Grey Label Brokerage in Under a Week

A week sounds ambitious, and in some cases it is. But brokers who show up prepared regularly go from signed agreement to live trading in five or six days. The ones who take a month usually aren’t held up by the technology. They’re held up by missing documents, undecided trading conditions, or a liquidity provider that hasn’t finished onboarding them.
So this guide covers two things: what happens during a MetaTrader grey label setup, and what you need sorted beforehand so the week actually stays a week.
Before Day One: What Has to Be Ready
This is the part people skip, and it’s the reason most timelines slip. A fast forex broker setup depends far more on your preparation than on your provider’s speed.
Before you sign anything, try to have these in place:
A registered company, plus a license or a clear regulatory route
A corporate bank account and at least one payment processor that will work with forex
A domain and a basic website, even a simple one
A rough idea of your target markets and client types
A liquidity provider you’ve spoken to, or are happy to take from your provider’s network
If you’re still waiting on any of these, the server can be ready long before your business is. That’s fine, but don’t count the week until these are close to done.
Step 1: Agree on Your Server Specs and Sign Off (Day 1)

Once you’ve chosen a provider, the first conversation is about the server itself. Which platform, MT5 or MT4 where it’s still available? Where should the server be hosted? Most brokers pick a data centre close to their liquidity, often London, New York or Singapore, to keep latency down.

You’ll also confirm what’s included: admin and manager terminals, backup servers, web and mobile terminals, and any plugins bundled in the package. Get this in writing. “I thought that was included” is a surprisingly common reason for delays on day four.
Step 2: Branding and Server Deployment (Days 1 to 2)

While the provider spins up your dedicated server, they’ll need your branding files. That usually means your company name as it should appear in the terminal, your logo in the formats they request, and the server name your clients will search for when they log in.
Choose the server name carefully. Clients will type it into a terminal, so keep it short and obvious. Something like YourBrand-Live and YourBrand-Demo works better than anything clever.
Deployment itself is often done within 24 to 48 hours. The work is mostly on the provider’s side, so this is a good time to get going on Step 3.
Step 3: Build Your Trading Conditions (Days 2 to 3)
This is where your input matters most, and where indecision costs the most time.
Symbols and Groups
Decide which instruments you’re offering at launch. Starting smaller is usually smarter: major and minor FX pairs, gold, maybe a handful of indices. You can add crypto CFDs or shares later.

Then set up your account groups. Most brokers launch with two or three account types, perhaps a standard account, a raw spread account with commission, and a demo group. Each group needs its own leverage, margin call and stop-out levels, swap settings and commission rules.
Execution Model

Will you send everything to liquidity (A-book), keep some flow in-house (B-book), or run a hybrid? This shapes how your bridge and risk tools get configured, so decide it now, not after launch. If you’re unsure, a hybrid model with clear routing rules is a common starting point, though it does need someone watching it.
Step 4: Connect Liquidity and the Bridge (Days 3 to 4)

With a grey label, you’re not locked into one liquidity source, which is a big part of why brokers choose it. Your provider connects your server to the liquidity provider through a bridge, then maps your symbols to theirs.

Expect a bit of back and forth here. Symbol naming, contract sizes and price precision all need to match. A small mismatch, like a gold contract set to 100 ounces on one side and 1 ounce on the other, can cause real trouble once live money is involved. Test every symbol, not just EURUSD.
Step 5: Plug In Your CRM, Payments and Client Area (Days 4 to 5)

Your traders won’t only see MetaTrader. They’ll see your client portal, where they register, upload KYC documents, deposit and withdraw. Most grey label providers either include a forex CRM or integrate one you already use.
On this step you’ll:
Connect the CRM to your MetaTrader server so accounts are created automatically
Add your payment gateways and test a few real deposits and withdrawals
Set up KYC rules that match what your regulator expects
Configure email notifications so they sound like your brand, not a template
Payments are often the slowest piece of the whole process, mostly because processors take their time approving forex merchants. If yours isn’t live yet, launch with bank wire and add cards later.
Step 6: Test Everything, Then Test It Again (Days 5 to 6)

Open a few live accounts with small amounts. Place trades on different symbols. Check that swaps calculate correctly overnight. Trigger a margin call on purpose. Make a withdrawal and time how long it takes.
Have someone who wasn’t involved in the setup try to break it. They’ll find the awkward spots your team has stopped noticing.
A Quick Pre-Launch Checklist
Admin and manager terminals working for your team
Backup server tested
Reports exporting properly for your back office and regulator
Risk alerts going to the right people
Support team trained on how the platform works and how to answer common client questions
Step 7: Go Live (Day 6 or 7)

Launch quietly. Bring in a small group of clients first, maybe from an IB you trust or your own network, and watch how the system handles real activity for a few days before you put money into marketing.
That soft launch is your safety net. Anything you missed in testing will show up here, while volumes are still small enough to fix calmly.
What Usually Slows Things Down
To be honest, it’s rarely the server. A MetaTrader grey label setup on the technical side can be finished in a few days by an experienced provider. Delays tend to come from:
Trading conditions that keep changing after configuration has started
Liquidity providers with slow onboarding
Payment processors still reviewing your application
Missing branding files or late sign-offs
Sort those out early and a one-week launch is realistic.
Conclusion

A fast forex broker setup comes down to preparation, quick decisions and a provider who has done this many times before. Get your business groundwork in order, know your trading conditions before day one, and leave enough time for proper testing.
If you’re planning your launch, MetaGreyLabel can take you through a timeline built around your markets, your liquidity and your launch date.

doc-38.title: Essential Tools and Plugins for a MetaTrader Grey Label Brokerage

blocks.text: Essential Tools and Plugins for a MetaTrader Grey Label Brokerage

Getting your own MetaTrader server is a big step. But on its own, a server is just an engine with no dashboard. What actually makes a brokerage run day to day is the set of tools and plugins sitting around it: the ones that route orders, flag risky clients, move money, and keep your regulator satisfied.

The good news with a grey label is that you get to pick those tools yourself. The less fun news is that it’s easy to overspend on extras you won’t touch for a year, or to launch without something you’ll badly need in week two. Here’s how to think about it.
Why Plugins Matter More on a Grey Label

On a white label, the host decides which add-ons run on the server, and you live with whatever they’ve picked. On a grey label, you have admin access, so you choose and configure your own stack. That freedom is a large part of the appeal, but it also means the job of choosing well now lands on you.
The right metatrader grey label plugins can mean the difference between a brokerage that runs itself most days and one where your team is fixing problems by hand at 2 a.m.
The Non-Negotiables
Some tools aren’t really optional. If you’re missing any of these at launch, you’ll notice quickly.
A Liquidity Bridge
This is the piece that connects your MetaTrader server to your liquidity providers. It takes client orders and sends them to the market, or routes them internally if you run a B-book or hybrid model.

When comparing bridges, look at execution speed, how many liquidity providers it can connect to at once, how flexible the routing rules are, and how much visibility you get into each fill. A good bridge lets you send larger or more toxic flow one way and smaller retail flow another, without someone having to step in manually.
A Forex CRM

Your CRM is where clients sign up, pass KYC, deposit, withdraw and manage their accounts. It’s also where your sales and support teams spend most of the day. It needs to sync properly with MetaTrader so accounts, balances and groups update automatically.
Pay attention to the client portal as well. Traders judge your brokerage by it more than you’d expect. If it’s slow or confusing, they assume your execution will be too.
Payment Gateway Integrations

You’ll want several ways for clients to fund their accounts: bank wire, cards, local payment methods, perhaps crypto where it’s allowed. Most of these connect through your CRM rather than straight to MetaTrader, but they belong on your list from day one. Clients who can’t deposit easily simply go somewhere else.
Risk Management Tools
This is the category new brokers tend to underestimate, and it’s where a lot of money is quietly lost or saved.

A proper risk tool gives your dealing desk a live view of exposure by symbol, by client and by group. It should flag unusual behaviour such as latency arbitrage, scalping on stale prices, or one client opening positions across several linked accounts.
Some brokers also add specialist plugins for:
Detecting toxic flow and moving those clients to A-book automatically
Setting exposure limits that adjust hedging as positions grow
Protecting against price spikes and bad ticks
Monitoring negative balances and handling them
If you run any B-book, risk tools aren’t a nice extra. They’re part of the core setup.
Back Office and Reporting
Regulators want reports, and so do your accountants. MetaTrader’s built-in reporting covers the basics, but most brokers outgrow it fast.

A back office tool pulls data from your server into clean reports on trading volume, deposits, P&L by group, IB commissions and so on. If you’re regulated, look for tools that can produce reports in the format your regulator expects. Building those by hand every month is miserable, and that’s when mistakes start to creep in.
Tools That Help You Grow
Once the basics are working, these are the forex broker tools that tend to bring in clients and keep them.
Copy Trading and PAMM/MAM

Copy trading lets less experienced clients follow successful traders automatically. PAMM and MAM systems let money managers trade on behalf of several investors from one master account. Both are popular, both increase volume, and both bring in clients who wouldn’t otherwise trade at all.
They do add complexity though, especially around fees, payouts and compliance. It’s worth waiting until your core operation runs smoothly before adding them.
IB and Affiliate Management

Introducing brokers are a major source of clients for many brokerages. An IB module tracks referrals, calculates rebates across multiple levels and pays out commissions without someone wrestling a spreadsheet every week. If IBs are part of your growth plan, get this in early. They notice errors in their payouts very quickly.
Extra Trading Tools for Clients

Things like advanced charting packages, trading signals, economic calendars and one-click trading add-ons. They aren’t essential, but they give your marketing team something to talk about and make your offering feel more complete than a bare terminal.
How to Choose Without Overbuying
It’s tempting to launch with everything. Resist that. Each plugin adds cost, setup time and one more thing that can break.
A sensible approach is to split your stack into three layers:
Launch essentials: bridge, CRM, payments, basic risk monitoring
First few months: reporting, IB module, stronger risk tools
Once you’re growing: copy trading, PAMM/MAM, extra client tools

Before you commit to any plugin, ask a few plain questions. Does it actually work with your MetaTrader version? Who supports it if something goes wrong at midnight? How is it priced, flat fee, per account or by volume? And can you switch it off or replace it later without rebuilding everything?
Integration Is the Real Test

One thing experienced brokers learn the hard way: a plugin that looks great in a demo can still be a headache if it doesn’t play nicely with the rest of your stack. Your CRM, bridge, risk tools and reporting all need to share data cleanly. When they don’t, you end up with mismatched balances, duplicate accounts and reports nobody trusts.

That’s why it often pays to work with a provider who has already tested common combinations of metatrader grey label plugins on live servers, rather than piecing together tools from five vendors who’ve never met.
Conclusion

The best stack isn’t the biggest one. It’s the one that fits your execution model, your markets and your team’s capacity right now, with room to add more later. Start with the essentials, get them working properly, then build out as your client base grows.
If you’re working out which forex broker tools make sense for your launch, MetaGreyLabel can help you put together a setup that suits where your brokerage is today.

doc-39.title: MetaTrader Grey Label Licensing: What It Includes and Why It Matters

blocks.text: MetaTrader Grey Label Licensing: What It Includes and Why It Matters

There’s a mix-up that comes up in almost every early conversation with new brokers. Someone hears “license” and assumes it means regulatory approval. It doesn’t. A metatrader grey label license is a technology arrangement. It gives you the right to run your own MetaTrader server under a provider’s master license. It says nothing about whether you’re allowed to offer trading services in a given country.
That distinction matters, and so does knowing exactly what you’re paying for. Here’s a clear look at both.
Two Very Different Kinds of License
When brokers talk about licensing, they’re usually mixing up two separate things.

The first is your financial or regulatory license. That comes from a regulator, whether that’s a tier-one body or an offshore authority, and it’s what makes your brokerage legal to operate. It covers things like capital requirements, client fund segregation, reporting and compliance staff.

The second is your platform license. That’s your right to use MetaTrader software commercially. MetaQuotes issues full licenses to brokers directly, but they’re costly and hard to get, and new MT4 licenses haven’t been available for years. A grey label is a way to get platform access without going down that route.
You need both. A grey label covers the technology side only. Any reputable provider will ask about your regulatory status before they set you up.
How a Grey Label License Actually Works

The provider holds a full MetaTrader license from MetaQuotes. Under that license, they deploy a dedicated server instance for your brokerage. It runs separately from other brokers, carries your branding, and you control it at admin level.
So you’re not technically the license holder in MetaQuotes’ eyes. Your provider is. But day to day, you’re running your own server with much of the control a full licensee would have.
That middle ground is where the name comes from. White label is fully shared and fully hosted. A full license is fully yours. Grey sits between the two.
What’s Typically Included
Packages vary between providers, so always read the agreement line by line. That said, most grey label arrangements cover something like this:
The Server and Its Infrastructure
A dedicated MetaTrader server instance, usually MT5
Hosting in a data centre of your choice, or one the provider recommends
A backup server for failover
Ongoing maintenance, security patches and platform updates from MetaQuotes
Terminals and Access
Administrator terminal, giving you full control of server settings
Manager terminals for your dealing desk, support and back office teams
Branded client terminals for desktop, web, iOS and Android
Your own server name, so clients search for your brand when they log in
Configuration Rights

This is where the real value sits. With admin access, you can set up symbols, groups, leverage, margin rules, swaps, commissions and execution settings yourself. You choose your liquidity providers. You can install plugins and connect third-party tools without asking the host for permission every time.
Support

Most providers include technical support, though the level differs a lot. Some offer round-the-clock monitoring. Others answer emails during office hours. Ask specifically what happens if your server has a problem on a Sunday night before the market opens.
What’s Usually Not Included
This catches people out. A grey label license generally does not include:
Your regulatory license or legal setup
Liquidity, which you contract separately, even if the provider introduces you
Bridge, CRM, risk tools or other plugins, unless they’re bundled
Payment processing
Your website and marketing
Some providers do offer bundles that bring several of these together. That can be convenient, but check each component’s pricing so you know what you’re really paying for.
The Real Grey Label License Benefits
So why do so many brokers go this way instead of a white label or a full license? The grey label license benefits come down to a few practical points.

Control without the full price. You get admin-level access and your own server for a fraction of what a full MetaQuotes license costs. For most mid-sized brokers, the full license simply isn’t worth it.

Freedom over liquidity and execution. You aren’t tied to the host’s liquidity or their way of handling orders. You can run A-book, B-book or hybrid on your own terms, and switch liquidity providers if pricing or fills get worse.
Your data stays separate. Client and trade data sit on your own server instance, not on a shared server with other brokers. Regulators and institutional partners tend to look more kindly on that.
Room to grow. As your volume increases, you can add plugins, adjust your setup and scale without migrating to a new platform. Many brokers stay on a grey label for years.
Faster launch than a full license. Getting a full license approved and built can take months. A grey label can be running in days once your paperwork is in order.
Questions to Ask Before You Sign
Since you’re relying on your provider’s master license, their reliability becomes your reliability. Before committing, it’s worth asking:
How long have they held their MetaQuotes license, and is it in good standing?
What happens to your server and client data if the agreement ends?
Can you migrate to another provider or to your own license later?
What exactly is covered in the monthly fee, and what costs extra?
What uptime do they guarantee, and what happens if they miss it?
The answer to the second question in particular tells you a lot. A provider confident in their service won’t make leaving painful.
Why It Matters for Your Brokerage

Your platform sits at the centre of everything. Clients trade on it, your dealers manage risk through it, and your reports come out of it. Choosing the wrong licensing setup can quietly limit how you price, how you execute and how quickly you can grow.

A metatrader grey label license isn’t the right fit for every brokerage. Very new brokers on tight budgets may be better off starting with a white label. But for brokers who want real control without taking on the cost and complexity of a full license, it’s often the most practical choice available.
Conclusion

Understand what you’re buying, keep platform licensing and regulatory licensing separate in your head, and read the agreement carefully. Do that, and the grey label license benefits become very clear in how your brokerage runs.

doc-40.title: How MetaTrader Grey Label Can Help You Attract More Forex Traders

blocks.text: How MetaTrader Grey Label Can Help You Attract More Forex Traders

Every broker says they offer tight spreads, fast execution and great support. Traders have heard it so often that it barely registers anymore. What actually wins clients these days is harder to fake: how the platform feels when they place a trade, how quickly a withdrawal arrives, and whether the account types fit how they really trade.

Most of that comes down to how much control you have over your setup. That’s where a grey label starts to earn its keep. It won’t market your brokerage for you, but it gives you the tools to build an offer that makes it far easier to attract forex traders and hold on to them.
Traders Already Know MetaTrader

Start with the obvious point. MetaTrader is the platform most retail traders learned on. They know where everything is, they have their favourite indicators set up, and many of them run Expert Advisors they’ve spent months tuning.

Ask them to switch to an unfamiliar platform and plenty will simply say no. Offer MetaTrader with your brand on it and you’ve removed one of the biggest reasons not to sign up. A grey label gives you exactly that, on a server that’s yours rather than one shared with a dozen other brokers.
Better Execution Is a Selling Point You Can Prove
Traders talk. On forums, in Telegram groups, on YouTube, they compare slippage, requotes and fill speeds between brokers. A reputation for poor execution spreads quickly and is hard to shake off.
With a grey label, you choose your own liquidity providers and configure your own bridge. That means you can:
Work with liquidity providers whose pricing and depth actually suit your clients
Route orders in a way that keeps fills clean
Host your server close to your liquidity to cut latency
Change providers if quality drops, instead of putting up with whatever a host offers

When your execution is genuinely good, you can show it. Publish execution stats, offer a demo that reflects real conditions, and let traders judge for themselves. Experienced traders trust that more than any slogan.
Account Types That Fit Different Traders

A scalper, a swing trader and a beginner on a small deposit all want different things. On a white label, you’re often limited to the account structures the host allows. On a grey label, you build them yourself.
Ideas That Tend to Work
A raw spread account with commission for active traders and EA users
A standard account with no commission and slightly wider spreads for newer clients
Swap-free accounts for traders who need them
Cent or micro accounts for people testing the water with small amounts
Different leverage options depending on regulation and client experience
Being able to tune each group, its margin levels, commissions, swaps and symbol list, lets you shape offers for specific audiences rather than one generic product that suits nobody especially well.
Features That Bring in New Kinds of Clients
Some traders don’t want to trade on their own at all. Others want to earn from their skills by managing money for followers. A grey label lets you add tools that reach these groups.
Copy Trading and Social Features

Copy trading appeals to people who are curious about forex but don’t have the time or confidence to trade themselves. They pick a strategy provider, set a risk level and let it run. For your brokerage, it’s a way to reach a much wider audience than active traders alone.
PAMM and MAM for Money Managers

Successful traders often want to manage funds for others. Giving them proper PAMM or MAM tools turns them into partners who bring their own investors with them. One good money manager can bring more volume than months of paid ads.
Partner and IB Programmes

Introducing brokers remain one of the most reliable ways to grow forex brokerage volume. With a grey label, you can connect a proper IB system with clear multi-level rebates and automated payouts. IBs stay loyal to brokers who pay accurately and on time, and they’re quick to leave the ones who don’t.
Trust Is a Growth Tool
Traders have become more cautious, and they’re right to be. They want to know their money is safe and that the broker isn’t working against them.

A grey label helps here in a few quiet ways. Your client data sits on your own server, not a shared one. You can show regulators and partners a cleaner, more transparent setup. And with your own branding on every terminal, your brokerage looks established rather than like a reseller of someone else’s platform.
None of that replaces proper regulation or honest marketing. But it supports both.
Fast Payments Keep Traders Around

This one isn’t strictly about MetaTrader, but it’s closely connected. With a grey label, your CRM and payment systems link directly to your own server, so deposits show up quickly and withdrawals can be processed without a host sitting in the middle.

Slow withdrawals are among the top reasons traders leave a broker and warn others away. Fast, predictable payouts do the opposite. Happy clients refer their friends, and that’s the cheapest acquisition channel there is.
Using Your Setup in Your Marketing
Having a strong platform only helps if people hear about it. A few ways brokers put their grey label setup to work:
Run demo competitions on your own server, with real prizes and leaderboards
Publish monthly execution reports showing average spreads and fill speeds
Create content around specific account types for specific trader groups
Feature successful strategy providers from your copy trading platform
Give IBs branded materials and tracking links that make promoting you easy
Each of these depends on having control over your server and your data, which is exactly what a grey label provides.
Where Growth Really Comes From

The brokers who manage to attract forex traders consistently aren’t usually the ones with the biggest ad budgets. They’re the ones whose product holds up when traders start using it. Clean execution, sensible account options, reliable withdrawals and useful tools turn first deposits into long-term clients.
A grey label won’t fix a weak business plan. But for brokers serious about building something lasting, it removes many of the limits that stop a brokerage from offering what traders want.
Conclusion

If you want to grow forex brokerage volume in a market this crowded, your platform has to be part of the pitch. Control over execution, accounts and features gives you something real to talk about, and something traders will notice once they’ve signed up.
If you’re looking at how a grey label could support your growth plans, MetaGreyLabel can help you map out a setup built around the traders you want to reach.

doc-41.title: Comparing MetaTrader Grey Label Providers: Features, Support and Prices

blocks.text: Comparing MetaTrader Grey Label Providers: Features, Support and Prices

On paper, most grey label providers look almost the same. Dedicated server, admin access, branded terminals, round-the-clock support. Read five websites back to back and you’d struggle to tell them apart.

The differences show up later. They appear when your server slows down during a news spike, when you need a plugin installed urgently, or when you find a fee in month three that nobody mentioned. So when brokers ask us about the best metatrader grey label providers, the honest answer is that it depends less on the brochure and more on what happens once you’re live.
Here’s how to compare providers properly, beyond the sales pitch.
Start With the Basics: Are They Legitimate?
Before you look at features or price, check the foundation. A grey label runs under your provider’s master MetaQuotes license. If their license has problems, so do you.

Ask how long they’ve held the license and whether it’s in good standing. Ask how many brokers they currently host and how long their oldest clients have been with them. A provider that’s been around for years with brokers who stay is a far safer bet than one with flashy pricing and no track record.

Also find out what happens if the provider runs into trouble. Can your server and client data be moved? Is there a clear exit process? You’d hope never to need it, but you want the answer before you sign.
Comparing Features
When you compare metatrader grey label offers, set up a simple table and score each provider against the same list. It stops one impressive feature from distracting you from gaps elsewhere.
Server and Infrastructure
Which platforms they offer: MT5 only, or MT4 as well where it’s still possible
Where they can host your server, and whether you get to choose
Whether a backup server is included or charged separately
How failover works if the main server goes down
Who handles MetaQuotes updates and how quickly they’re rolled out
Access and Control

Check that you’re actually getting full administrator access, not a limited admin role with some settings locked. Some providers quietly restrict what you can change. Ask directly which settings you can’t touch.
Also find out how many manager terminals are included. A growing dealing desk, support team and back office can need more than you’d think.
Integrations and Plugins

Find out which bridges, CRMs, risk tools and liquidity providers they’ve already integrated. A provider with tested connections saves you weeks of troubleshooting. One that says “we can integrate anything” without examples may be learning on your server.
Ask too whether you can bring your own tools, or whether they push you towards their in-house products.
Comparing Support
Support is where providers differ most, and where it’s hardest to judge before you sign.
What to Ask
What hours is technical support actually available, including weekends before the market opens?
Is there live monitoring of your server, or do they only respond once you report a problem?
What are their response times for urgent issues, and are they written into the agreement?
Will you have a named account manager, or will each ticket go to whoever is free?
Do they help with configuration, such as setting up groups and symbols, or is that entirely on you?
How to Test It

Don’t just take their word for it. Send a few technical questions before signing and see how quickly and clearly they reply. Ask for references from current brokers, and actually call them. Ask those brokers about the worst problem they’ve had and how the provider dealt with it. That one answer will tell you more than any sales call.
Comparing Prices
Grey label pricing is rarely as simple as one monthly number. Providers bundle and split costs in different ways, so lining up headline prices side by side can mislead you.
Common Cost Elements
One-time setup fee
Monthly server and license fee
Charges per active account, or based on trading volume
Backup server fees
Extra manager terminals
Plugin and integration costs
Charges for custom development or configuration work
Reading Between the Lines

A low setup fee sometimes comes with high volume-based charges, which can get expensive once you start growing. A higher flat fee might work out cheaper over two or three years. Ask each provider to estimate your total cost at three points: at launch, at your expected volume after a year, and at a stretch target. That gives you a far more honest comparison than the opening price.
Also check the contract length and notice period. A cheap deal that locks you in for three years with a heavy exit fee isn’t really cheap.
Red Flags to Watch For
A few warning signs come up again and again:
Pricing that changes depending on who you speak to
Vague answers about who actually holds the MetaQuotes license
No clear process for moving your data if you leave
Pressure to sign quickly because of a “limited offer”
Reluctance to put you in touch with existing clients
Support contacts that turn out to be a single email address
Any one of these is worth questioning. Several together usually mean walking away.
Matching the Provider to Your Brokerage

The best metatrader grey label providers for a new broker aren’t necessarily the best for an established one. If you’re just starting, you might value hands-on configuration help and a simple, predictable fee. If you’re already running volume, deep integrations, strong risk tools and solid uptime guarantees matter more.
Be honest about where you are now and where you expect to be in a year. Pick the provider that fits that path, not the one with the longest feature list.
Conclusion

When you compare metatrader grey label providers, look past the website and test what matters: the license behind the service, the support you’ll get when things go wrong, and the full cost over time. A careful week of comparison can save you a painful migration later.

doc-42.title: MetaTrader Grey Label + CRM Integration: Boosting Client Onboarding and Retention

blocks.text: MetaTrader Grey Label + CRM Integration: Boosting Client Onboarding and Retention

Here’s something brokers often find out too late. You can have excellent execution, tight spreads and a well-run server, and still lose clients before they place a single trade. They sign up, hit a clunky KYC form, wait two days for an account, struggle to deposit, and quietly give up.

Most of that friction has nothing to do with MetaTrader itself. It happens in the space between your website, your back office and your trading server. That’s what a proper forex crm integration is meant to fix.
What the CRM Actually Does in a Brokerage
In a forex brokerage, the CRM is far more than a contact list. It’s the system that handles almost everything a client does outside the trading terminal:
Registration and identity verification
Creating live and demo accounts
Deposits, withdrawals and internal transfers
Support tickets and communication
IB and affiliate tracking
Sales pipelines and lead management
Your clients see the client portal. Your team sees the back office. Underneath, the CRM keeps both connected to your MetaTrader server.
Why Integration Matters More on a Grey Label

With a white label, you’re often stuck with whatever CRM the host supports, connected however they’ve decided to connect it. With a grey label, you run your own server with admin access, so you can integrate the CRM properly and decide how data flows between the two.

A well-built metatrader grey label crm connection means accounts get created automatically, balances update in real time, group changes happen without anyone typing them in, and your team can see a client’s full picture in one place. Done badly, you end up with staff copying numbers between systems and clients asking why their deposit hasn’t shown up.
How Integration Improves Onboarding
The first few days of a client’s relationship with you matter enormously. Most drop-off happens right here.
Faster Account Opening

When your CRM is linked directly to your MetaTrader server, a client can register, pass verification and receive login details within minutes. No manual step where someone in your back office creates the account by hand and emails credentials the next morning.
That speed matters. A trader who signs up while excited about a setup they’ve spotted wants to trade now, not tomorrow.
Smoother KYC

Good CRMs let clients upload documents straight from their phone, run automatic ID checks where your regulator allows it, and flag only the cases that really need a human to review. Your compliance team spends its time on the tricky files instead of approving obvious ones.
Deposits That Just Work

Payment gateways connect through the CRM. When everything is integrated, a deposit made through the portal lands in the client’s MetaTrader balance automatically. No waiting, no support ticket asking where the money went.
This is often the single biggest factor in whether a new client goes on to trade. Make the first deposit easy and most of the battle is won.
How Integration Improves Retention
Getting a client through the door is only half the job. Keeping them is where long-term revenue comes from.
A Full View of Every Client

With your CRM pulling trading data from MetaTrader, your team can see not just who a client is, but how they trade. Deposit history, trading frequency, favourite instruments, open positions, recent losses.

That context changes how you support people. A client who has gone quiet for two weeks after a run of losing trades needs a different conversation from one who just made their third deposit in a month.
Automated, Relevant Communication

Integration lets you trigger messages based on real behaviour. A welcome sequence for new accounts. A reminder for clients who registered but never funded. A note about a new account type for traders who’d clearly benefit from it.
The key word is relevant. Clients ignore generic newsletters but respond to messages that clearly fit their situation.
Quicker Withdrawals

Nothing hurts retention like slow withdrawals. When your CRM, payments and MetaTrader server are all connected, withdrawal requests can be checked, approved and processed far faster. Fast, reliable payouts build the kind of trust that keeps clients around and gets them recommending you.
Support That Knows the Context

When a client contacts support, your agent should be able to see their account, recent trades and payment history straight away. No asking for login numbers, no transferring between departments. Small thing, big difference in how people feel about your brokerage.
The IB Side of the Equation

If introducing brokers are part of your growth plan, integration matters even more. Your CRM needs accurate trade data from MetaTrader to calculate rebates correctly. When the two are properly linked, commissions are worked out automatically and IBs can follow their earnings in their own portal.
Get it wrong and you’ll spend hours fixing disputes. IBs talk to each other, and a reputation for unreliable payouts spreads fast.
What to Look for in a CRM Integration
Not every CRM connects equally well. When assessing options, ask:
Does it support your MetaTrader version and work with grey label servers?
Is the connection real time, or does data sync in batches?
Can it handle several servers, such as separate live and demo environments?
How does it deal with errors, like a failed deposit or a duplicate account?
Is the client portal mobile-friendly and easy to brand?
Can it grow with you as you add copy trading, PAMM or more payment methods?
Ask for a demo using a test MetaTrader server, not just slides. Watching an account being created, funded and traded end to end tells you more than any feature list.
Common Mistakes to Avoid
A few things trip brokers up regularly:
Launching before payment gateways are properly tested through the CRM
Mismatched group names between the CRM and MetaTrader, causing accounts to land in the wrong group
Too many manual approval steps that slow onboarding for no real compliance reason
Not training support staff on the back office before going live
Each is easy to fix early and painful to fix later.
Conclusion

Your trading platform gets clients to trade. Your CRM gets them to sign up, fund and stay. A solid forex crm integration ties the two together so clients have a smooth experience from registration to withdrawal, and your team spends less time fixing data and more time helping people.
